reason: Only dev scripts under extras/ (CreateConceptSet.R:32, TestConcepts.R:129) reference the moved file; they are ad hoc scripts with hardcoded server names, still unchanged at HEAD, and no package code or test is affected.
Sccs.sql:233 in the new 'dx' branch selects from #custom_coviariate_ids while R uploads #custom_covariate_ids (DataLoadingSaving.R:158), so the INSERT fails when has_custom_covariate_ids is set.
Bare `return` is sloppy but test_EndToEnd.R only calls createCohortSet() for its side effect and never uses `cohorts`, so nothing breaks.
The postgres migration is valid (SELECT without FROM is legal in Postgres, nextval on the sequence); the flagged parse failure is just the ohdsiSchema Flyway placeholder.
Standard Circe-generated SqlRender cohort SQL with @params and #temp tables; it is not parseable by a plain parser but is valid input for SqlRender.
global.R:129 uses dbms = database in the user-settings branch where database is never defined; a later commit f7459aff 'Fixed bug in connections' changed it to dbms = dbms.

The commit uppercases the DX_CATEGORY values in the codes table (lines 224-245) while the filters at lines 302/315/333 still compare to lowercase; Oracle compares case-sensitively and a later commit 4439318 'caps issue' addressed it.

Migration_2 does ALTER COLUMN row_count BIGINT without NOT NULL, which on SQL Server makes it nullable, contradicting the spec (row_count required) and ResultTables.sql; no later migration restores NOT NULL. Impact limited to non-Postgres backends.
type_float renders as float/double precision on Postgres where round(double precision, int) does not exist; the next commit ffd2bd3 'try 4' switched to dbt.type_numeric.

The query is a spot-check list of sites from the jamstack_sites table for the methodology/date; bare LIMIT is arbitrary rather than random but it is a draft helper with no downstream consumer and unchanged since.
The 0.1 default is a deliberate patch for Eunomia test data per the commit message and was kept in later commits (b355e27, now 0.01 'set default for eunomia data').
At this commit DESCRIPTION did not list CohortGenerator, which tests/testthat/setup.R calls; a later commit (84cd855 and neighbours) added it to Suggests/Remotes. Minor test-environment defect.
The commit renames total_spent to total_messages_spent in twilio__account_overview.sql:38 but twilio.yml:156 still documents total_spent; the docs were fixed in later commits (4dc8193, f7c9974).
The clone shows blocks.py and transactions.py as .REMOVED.git-id stubs under op_datasets/schemas; the commit moved the real files there, so the import resolves in the actual repo.
Standard Circe-generated SqlRender cohort SQL (#Codesets, @vocabulary_database_schema); not a defect.
unique-company-names.sql generated by generate-company-name-sql.ts ends each statement with `in (...));` and 44 of 47 statements have unbalanced parentheses, so they are syntax errors.
Standard Circe-generated cohort SQL with SqlRender syntax; not a defect.
Auto-synced catalog metadata (metadata.json update_frequency changed to Nunca in the same commit); documentation text only, not code behaviour.
`UPDATE TABLE <t> SET` is invalid syntax; later history on this file (53eeb16 'Fix bug in migration') replaced it with `UPDATE <t> SET is_templated_cohort = 0`.
global.R:299 assigns x$phenotype_id <- cohort[i,]$phenotypeId inside a loop over phenotypeDescription rows, attaching the wrong phenotype id (should index phenotypeDescription).
Valid TiDB/MySQL SQL with use index hints; the hardcoded repo_id is replaced via the params.json replaces mechanism, not a defect.
The generator emits `in (...));` with an extra closing paren after the already-balanced trim(replace(...)), so every company UPDATE is a syntax error.
Left-joining one row per synonym name is the intended design (column renamed to referent, then pivoted into metadata rows), not an accidental fan-out.
Requiring the dotenv file is a deliberate design of this new package (load_env raises by intent); no workflow at this commit imports op_coreutils, and it was only removed later when containerising.
